nodes.summary: For a finite set $A$ of points in the Euclidean plane, call a distance $k$-rich for $A$ if at least $k$ unordered pairs of distinct points of $A$ lie at that distance, and let $f(n)$ be the largest number of $(n+1)$-rich distances of a set of $n$ points. Then there is a constant $C$ with $n \le C f(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$; for every $n$ there is a set of $n$ points with at least $\lfloor n/4 \rfloor$…
nodes.title: Bhowmick's theorem on rich distances

nodes.summary: For a finite set $X$ of points in the Euclidean plane and $x \in X$, let $R_X(x)$ be the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\alpha_k$ be the infimum of the reals $c$ for which there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some set $X$ of exactly $n$ points in the plane has at least $k$ points $x$ with $R_X(x) < c\sqrt{n}$ (an empty set or a set unbounded below…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 652 is true

nodes.summary: For a finite set $X$ of points in the Euclidean plane and $x \in X$, let $R_X(x)$ be the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\alpha_k$ be the infimum of the reals $c$ for which there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some set $X$ of exactly $n$ points in the plane has at least $k$ points $x$ with $R_X(x) < c\sqrt{n}$ (an empty set or a set unbounded below…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 652

nodes.summary: For a finite set $X$ of points in the Euclidean plane and a real number $t$, the number of points $x \in X$ such that the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$ is less than $t$.
nodes.title: Points with few distinct distances

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a finite set of points in a metric space and let $d$ be a real number. The multiplicity of $d$ in $P$ is the number of unordered pairs $\{p, q\}$ of distinct points of $P$ with $\operatorname{dist}(p, q) = d$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a distance

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in a metric space, the distance set of $P$ is the finite set of real numbers $\operatorname{dist}(p, q)$ with $p$ and $q$ distinct points of $P$.
nodes.title: Distance set of a finite point set

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in a metric space and a point $x$ of the space, this is the number of distinct values $\operatorname{dist}(y, x)$ with $y$ a point of $P$ other than $x$.
nodes.title: Number of distinct distances from a point

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in a metric space, the number of distinct distances of $P$ is the number of elements of its distance set, that is, the number of distinct values $\operatorname{dist}(p, q)$ with $p$ and $q$ distinct points of $P$.
nodes.title: Number of distinct distances

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $\alpha_k$ is the infimum of the set of real numbers that are admissible for $k$: the reals $c$ for which there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some set $X$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean plane contains at least $k$ points $x$ such that the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$ is less than $c\sqrt{n}$. If this set is empty or unbounded below,…
nodes.title: The Erdős constant $\alpha_k$

nodes.summary: There is a real number $\delta > 0$ such that for every natural number $N$ there are an integer $n \ge N$ and a set $P$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with at least $n^{1+\delta}$ unordered pairs of points of $P$ at distance exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Erdős's unit distance conjecture is false

nodes.summary: There is a real constant $C$ such that for every nonempty finite set $A$ of points of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^4$ and every natural number $f$, if for every $x \in A$ there is a real number $r > 0$ such that at least $f$ points of $A$ lie at distance $r$ from $x$, then $f \le |A|/2 + C$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 754: favourite distances in $\mathbb{R}^4$

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there is a real constant $C$ such that for every nonempty finite set $A$ of points of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^4$ and every natural number $f$, if for every $x \in A$ there is a real number $r > 0$ such that at least $f$ points of $A$ lie at distance $r$ from $x$, then $f \le |A|/2 + C$. Equivalently, $f(n) \le n/2 + O(1)$, where $f(n)$ is the largest $f$ such that some set $A$ of…
nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 754

nodes.summary: There is a real constant $C$ such that for every sufficiently large natural number $n$ there is a set $P$ of $n$ points of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every $4$-element subset of $P$ determines at least $3$ distinct distances and $P$ determines at most $C n / \sqrt{\log n}$ distinct distances.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 659: few distances with every four points spanning three

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there is a real constant $C$ such that for every sufficiently large natural number $n$ there is a set $P$ of $n$ points of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every $4$-element subset of $P$ determines at least $3$ distinct distances and $P$ determines at most $C n / \sqrt{\log n}$ distinct distances.
nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 659

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and a real number $c$, the property that some set $X$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean plane contains at least $k$ points $x$ such that the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$ is less than $c\sqrt{n}$.
nodes.title: Many points with few distinct distances

nodes.summary: A real number $c$ is admissible for $k \in \mathbb{N}$ if there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some set $X$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean plane contains at least $k$ points $x$ such that the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$ is less than $c\sqrt{n}$.
nodes.title: Admissible constants in Erdős Problem 652

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the largest, over all sets $A$ of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane, of the number of rich distances of $A$ at level $n + 1$, that is, of distances that occur for at least $n + 1$ unordered pairs of distinct points of $A$.
nodes.title: Maximal number of rich distances

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space and $n$ a natural number such that $X$ contains a set of exactly $n$ points. The minimum number of distinct distances for $n$ points in $X$ is the least number of distinct distances determined by a set of exactly $n$ points of $X$.
nodes.title: Minimum number of distinct distances

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and a real number $\delta$, this is the number of unordered pairs $\{p, q\}$ of distinct points $p, q \in P$ with Euclidean distance $|p - q| = \delta$, computed as half the number of ordered pairs $(p, q)$ of distinct points of $P$ at distance $\delta$ and taken as a real number.
nodes.title: Number of pairs at a given distance

nodes.summary: The real Euclidean plane is the space $\mathbb{R}^2$ of pairs of real numbers with the Euclidean inner product and norm.
nodes.title: Euclidean plane for Erdős Problem 652

nodes.summary: For a finite set $A$ of points in the Euclidean plane and a natural number $k$, the rich distances of $A$ at level $k$ are the distances $d$ between two distinct points of $A$ such that at least $k$ unordered pairs of distinct points of $A$ are at distance $d$.
nodes.title: Rich distances

nodes.summary: There is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there are a set $P$ of $n$ distinct points on the unit sphere $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \|x\| = 1\}$ and a real number $\delta$ for which the number of unordered pairs of distinct points of $P$ at distance $\delta$ is at least $f(n) \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 605 is true

nodes.summary: The proposition that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there are a set $P$ of $n$ distinct points on the unit sphere $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \|x\| = 1\}$ and a real number $\delta$ for which the number of unordered pairs of distinct points of $P$ at distance $\delta$ is at least $f(n) \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 605 (repeated distances on the sphere)

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, the number of unit-distance pairs of $P$ is the number of unordered pairs of points of $P$ at distance exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Number of unit-distance pairs in a planar point set

nodes.summary: For a finite set of $n$ points in a metric space, the number of unit distances is at most $\binom{n}{2}$, the total number of unordered pairs of distinct points.
nodes.title: Trivial upper bound on unit distances

nodes.summary: For a finite set $S$ of points in a metric space, the number of unit distances of $S$ is the number of unordered pairs $\{p, q\}$ of points of $S$ with $\operatorname{dist}(p, q) = 1$, that is, the multiplicity of the distance $1$ in $S$.
nodes.title: Number of unit distances

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, the unit distance count of $P$ is the number of unordered pairs of points of $P$ at distance exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Unit distance count of a planar point set

nodes.summary: There is a constant $C > 0$ such that every finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ has at most $C n^{4/3}$ unordered pairs of points at distance exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter unit distance bound

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
